title: Adverse respiratory effect of acute beta-blocker exposure in asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Morales DR, Jackson C, Lipworth BJ, Donnan PT, Guthrie B
population: Randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled trials of acute beta-blocker exposure in people with asthma
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central.
result: Acute selective beta-blockers changed FEV1 by a mean -6.9% (95% CI -8.5 to -5.2), lowered FEV1 by 20% or more in one in eight patients, caused symptoms in one in 33 and attenuated the response to a beta2-agonist by 10.2% (-14.0 to -6.4). For acute non-selective beta-blockers the corresponding values were -10.2% (-14.7 to -5.6), one in nine, one in 13 and -20.0% (-29.4 to -10.7). A dose-response relationship was shown for selective beta-blockers, and celiprolol and labetalol differed from the others.
